traditions.author: Tulsīdās
traditions.role: comparison telling, Awadhi — widely known to Hindi-speaking audiences
traditions.section: Bālkāṇḍ, after dohā 205 — विश्वामित्र का राजा दशरथ से राम-लक्ष्मण को माँगना
traditions.source: Ramcharitmanas text in common circulation (Gita Press recension); verses quoted from public presentations
traditions.not: Not the default. The default is the identified Vālmīki spine. No regional telling has been chosen as canonical for any language.

divergences.gloss: Mārīca and Subāhu disturb the sage's rites — the same two, same act.
Viśvāmitra asks for Rāma because he KNOWS Rāma is Hari incarnate — 'without Hari these demons will not die.'
divergences.divergence: In Vālmīki he asks for a capable prince and says nothing of divinity. Tulsī makes the request theological. Our films follow the spine: the sage asks for a boy he is certain of, not for a god he has recognised.

divergences.gloss: 'Where are those terrible cruel rākṣasas, and where is my tender son of very young age' — the father's refusal, same beat, different words.
divergences.note: Confirms the emotional shape of film 3 across both traditions.

divergences.gloss: Hearing the king's love-soaked words, the wise sage was DELIGHTED in his heart. Then Vasiṣṭha explained at length.
divergences.divergence: MAJOR. In Vālmīki the sage is angered (samanyuḥ) and the earth shakes (⟨Bāla 20.4, GRETIL — text withheld⟩, Bāla 20.4). In Tulsī he is pleased by the father's love and there is no anger at all. Film 5 — 'The Sage's Anger' — exists only in the spine.
divergences.consequence: A Hindi viewer raised on Tulsī may not recognise the anger. Ask must answer this the moment it is asked, and the film must never imply the anger is universal.

divergences.gloss: 'The two beautiful brothers, dark and fair' — Rāma śyāma, Lakṣmaṇa gaura.
divergences.consequence: A Tradition-class datum for the complexion locks. Corroborates dark Rāma, but the spine's own term must still be located and verified before L-RAMA is unlocked. Tradition never substitutes for Text.

divergences.gloss: With a single arrow he took her life, and knowing her wretched, gave her his own abode.
divergences.divergence: Tulsī grants Tāṭakā liberation at death. Vālmīki does not. A devotional softening of the killing — and directly relevant to the Tāṭakā memo.
divergences.handling: Separately attributed telling difference. NOT added to default narration, visuals or the causal graph. No decision to blend traditions is made. Surfaced only if a viewer asks.

divergences.gloss: The sage gave the knowledge by which hunger and thirst do not come — bala and atibala, as in the spine (Bāla 21.10–15).
